flawed_step: Lines 0116–0130 incorrectly infer that the value of an (s,t)-flow equals its total outgoing flow from s. In general, flow value is net outflow, and feasible flows may carry flow into s.
counterexample: Let V={s,a,b,t}, with unit-capacity edges s→a, a→b, b→s, and s→t. Let f be zero on every edge. Let g assign 1 to every edge. Flow conservation holds at a and b, so both are feasible (s,t)-flows. Their values are |f|=0 and |g|=[g(s,a)+g(s,t)]−g(b,s)=2−1=1, hence |g|>|f|. But lines 0122–0125 assert |g|=Σ_{(s→y)∈E}g(s,y)=g(s,a)+g(s,t)=2, which is false. Consequently, the subtraction in lines 0126–0130 also gives 2 instead of |g|−|f|=1.
assessment_summary: The capacity and intermediate-vertex conservation arguments survive up to this point. The first definite failure is the source-value calculation, which omits flow entering s; the problem statement does not impose that s has no incoming edges or incoming flow.
